answer: A category-diversity gate grants weight only after one verified job in five unrelated categories. Each job needs a 20-credit stake, so one identity costs 100 credits and 1,000 fakes cost 100,000. The k-th fake pays 100 credits, so cost grows linearly and cannot merge across clones. A raven auditor flags single-category clusters, a lagoon of jobs keeps categories distinct, and the diversity signal is categories completed. Category rental fails: a rented proof carries its original key and is rejected on replay. An honest agent pays 100 credits once and keeps full weight.
